region: Karakoram Highway and Hunza, Lahore and the Punjab forts, Sindh and Cholistan
title: Pakistan — The Karakoram Highway and the Mughal and Indus Heartlands
subtitle: A concept of high Karakoram valleys, Lahore's Mughal city and Bronze Age Mohenjo-daro, not currently recommendable
summary: Pakistan combines the Hunza and Skardu valleys, Lahore's Mughal heritage and Indus Valley sites, but official advice is orange or red for every part of the route and terrorism risk is raised, so it is excluded.
introduction: Pakistan packs several expeditions into one country: the Karakoram Highway climbing from the Indus into the Hunza Valley beneath 7,000 m peaks, Lahore's Walled City with the Badshahi Mosque and Wazir Khan Mosque, the 16th-century Rohtas Fort in the Salt Range, Gandharan monasteries at Taxila, the Bronze Age streets of Mohenjo-daro, Makli's tombs near the Indus delta and Derawar Fort in the Cholistan Desert. In February and March the high north is cold and the Khunjerab Pass is closed, so the lowland heritage would carry the trip. Security, however, rules the whole concept out for now.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is a self-drive, tented trip across dry wadis and dunes with a single dominant landscape. Pakistan would be a hired-driver trip through 4,500 years of urban history and the world's highest paved border road, with almost no wild camping.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: The usual package is a Lahore-Islamabad-Hunza coach tour in summer. A winter loop through forts, desert castles and the Indus plain would be much less visited, but is also the part of the country where official advice is strictest.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Only Pakistan combines Mughal Lahore, the Indus Valley civilisation and the Karakoram in one country; Iraq and Egypt offer ancient cities, Taiwan and Yunnan offer mountains, none offers all three.

recommendedTravelWindow.window: Mid to late March 2027, after Eid al-Fitr
recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Lowland Punjab and Sindh are warm but not hot in March and Ramadan ends around 9 March, but the Khunjerab Pass and high roads of the north may still be closed or snowy. Purely informational because the route is excluded.

februarySuitability.summary: Ramadan from about 8 February; cold and snowbound in the north with weather-dependent flights to Skardu and Gilgit; lowlands are pleasant.

marchSuitability.summary: Mild to warm lowlands, with Hunza still cold and the Khunjerab Pass normally closed until around 1 April; Ramadan ends about 9 March.

climate.regionNote: Rounded climate-normal estimates for Lahore and Islamabad (lowlands); the north is far colder. Not a 2027 forecast and not taken from a verified station table.

february.rainfall: Some winter rain in the Punjab; snow in Hunza and Skardu.
february.notes: Hunza and Skardu roughly -8 to 8 C; fog and smog in the plains.

march.notes: Hunza roughly -2 to 14 C; Sindh and Cholistan reach 30 C.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Khunjerab Pass is generally closed to all vehicles 30 Dec-1 Apr and heavy snow can shut the Karakoram Highway for extended periods (S05, S06).
climate.airQuality: Lahore and the Punjab plains suffer winter smog, usually worst November to January and easing by March.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Deosai and the north are snowbound in winter; migratory birds are present in the Indus wetlands.

geography.summary: The Indus drains from the Karakoram through the Punjab plains to a delta on the Arabian Sea, with the Salt Range, Cholistan and the Thar desert on the side.
geography.distinctive: The Karakoram Highway follows the Indus and Hunza gorges between the Karakoram, the Hindu Kush and the Himalaya, and passes the Attabad Lake created by a 2010 landslide.

signatureExperiences.title: Karakoram Highway into Hunza
signatureExperiences.description: Fly to Gilgit or Skardu and drive the Hunza Valley to Karimabad and Attabad Lake.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the great mountain roads, with an abandoned highway section beneath a lake.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Domestic flight Islamabad-Gilgit or Skardu, then hired driver; flights are weather dependent and the road section south of Chilas is against all travel (S02).

signatureExperiences.title: Lahore Walled City and its Mughal monuments
signatureExperiences.description: Lahore Fort, Badshahi Mosque, Wazir Khan Mosque and the food streets.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the densest Mughal ensembles in the world, with a living food culture.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local guide and driver; avoid crowds and gatherings (S01).

signatureExperiences.title: Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Valley
signatureExperiences.description: Walk the streets of a Bronze Age city and the tombs of Makli.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Among the earliest planned cities in the world.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Flight to Sukkur or Karachi and hired driver; Sindh north of Nawabshah is against all but essential travel (S02).

security.summary: Excluded: France Diplomatie classes every part of the route as orange or red (Punjab outside the Lahore-Islamabad-Faisalabad triangle is red), the UK advises against all or all-but-essential travel for the Karakoram Highway south of Chilas and for northern Sindh, and terrorism risk has risen since the Pakistan-Afghanistan clashes.
security.assessedRoute: Islamabad, Taxila, Rohtas Fort, Lahore, Cholistan (Derawar), Mohenjo-daro, Makli/Thatta, Gilgit, Hunza (Karimabad, Attabad) and Skardu.

advisories.level: Red (formally discouraged): Balochistan, ex-FATA, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab except the Faisalabad-Lahore-Islamabad triangle, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Indian border; orange (discouraged except for compelling reasons) elsewhere, incl. Sindh, Gilgit-Baltistan and the triangle (zones updated 11 Mar 2026; page 25 Sep 2026)
advisories.routeImpact: Every stop is in an orange or red zone; Rohtas Fort and Derawar Fort are in red Punjab.

advisories.level: Against all travel: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Karakoram Highway Mansehra-Chilas, Balochistan, 10 miles of the Afghan border and Line of Control; against all but essential travel: Sindh north of and including Nawabshah, Azad Kashmir, Dera Ghazi Khan, 5 miles of the Indian border (updated 18 Nov 2026)
advisories.regionsAffected: Karakoram Highway south of Chilas, northern Sindh
advisories.routeImpact: Mohenjo-daro is in northern Sindh and the overland road to Hunza passes the against-all section.

advisories.level: Red: KP, Balochistan and borders; orange: Sindh, most of Punjab, Kashmir, most of Gilgit-Baltistan; yellow: Islamabad, Lahore, Hunza Valley, Gilgit, Skardu (valid to 28 Nov 2026)
advisories.regionsAffected: Sindh and most of Punjab orange
advisories.routeImpact: Lahore and Hunza are yellow, but Sindh and Rohtas-Derawar areas are orange.

advisories.level: Level 3: Reconsider travel (armed conflict, terrorism, crime, kidnapping)

conflictRisk.note: Armed clashes with Afghanistan since 26 Feb 2026 and recurrent exchanges of fire on the Line of Control and Indian border (S01).

terrorismRisk.note: Suicide attacks in Islamabad on 11 Nov 2025 and 6 Feb 2026; attacks target hotels, markets and tourist spots (S01, S04).

kidnappingRisk.note: Cited by the US advisory (S04); not mentioned by France or the UK pages as fetched.

regionalRestrictions: Wagah and Kartarpur crossings to India closed (S02)
Protests may bring phone and mobile data cuts (S01, S04)
ordinaryRisks: Winter snow and landslides on the Karakoram Highway
security.medicalAccess: Good private hospitals in Lahore and Islamabad; limited in the mountains.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Many insurers exclude destinations under government advice against travel; cover for French orange or red zones is doubtful.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure. Reconsider only if France moves the Lahore-Islamabad corridor and Gilgit-Baltistan to yellow and the UK keeps the north unlisted.

practicalRequirements.visa: Conditional on nationality; an online visa exists but the official portal returned HTTP 403, so rules and fees are not verified.
permits: NOC may be required for some areas (S01); rules not verified
practicalRequirements.insurance: Check that the policy covers destinations under advice against travel; likely void.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Local SIMs available; shutdowns during protests.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cash widely used; card acceptance limited outside big cities.
practicalRequirements.medical: Check vaccinations with a travel clinic.
